identity.title: Prodrome before loss of consciousness (nausea, warmth, diaphoresis, visual graying) and situational trigger (micturition, cough, prolonged standing, pain, post-prandial) vs none

technique.how: Ask what the patient felt in the seconds to minutes before losing consciousness (nausea, warmth, sweating, vision graying or tunnelling, sounds fading) and how long it lasted; then ask about the setting (prolonged standing, heat, pain or emotion, micturition, defecation, cough, after a meal). Ask witnesses about pallor and sweating.
technique.prerequisites: Patient or witness able to recall the event; ask before suggesting symptom lists to reduce leading.

interpretation.positive_finding: A prolonged autonomic prodrome (nausea, diaphoresis, blurred vision) and a classic situational trigger point toward reflex (vasovagal/situational) or orthostatic syncope and make cardiac syncope less likely (nausea LR+ for cardiac ~0.4; long prodrome ~0.6).
interpretation.negative_finding: Absent or very brief prodrome modestly raises the likelihood of cardiac (arrhythmic) syncope (LR ~1.7 for absent long prodrome), especially with structural heart disease, exertion, or supine onset.
interpretation.pitfalls: Older patients frequently have amnesia for the prodrome and cardiac syncope can be preceded by lightheadedness, so prodrome presence is a modest discriminator; palpitations before syncope are inconsistent across studies. Individual RCE items with strong LRs (mood change, feeling cold, headache) are rarely present.
interpretation.changes_what: Typical prodrome plus trigger: favor reflex/orthostatic cause and consider discharge if ECG normal; absent prodrome pushes toward monitoring/cardiac evaluation.

estimates.population: Pooled derivation sample from 7 studies (n=2388) of adults with syncope; finding = presence/prolonged presence of prodromal symptoms or awareness of being about to faint
estimates.reference_standard: Final adjudicated cause of syncope in each primary study (cardiac vs non-cardiac)
estimates.computed_from: Cardiac: 182 with prodrome / 468 (39%); non-cardiac: 1117 / 1768 (63%). LR+ = 0.389/0.632 = 0.62; LR- = 0.611/0.368 = 1.66 (table reports LR 1.66 for absence). Spec = 1-0.63.

estimates.population: Pooled derivation sample from 6 studies reporting nausea before syncope in adults with syncope
estimates.reference_standard: Final adjudicated cause of syncope in each primary study

estimates.population: Pooled derivation sample from 6 studies reporting diaphoresis before syncope in adults with syncope
estimates.reference_standard: Final adjudicated cause of syncope in each primary study

estimates.population: Adults with syncope (n=412) from RCE-pooled studies; prodromal symptom of feeling cold
estimates.reference_standard: Cardiac syncope by independent reference standard in included studies
estimates.quote: feeling cold (n = 412; sensitivity, 2% [95% CI, 0%-5%]; specificity, 89% [95% CI, 85%-93%]; LR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06-0.64])

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a reassuring prodrome to skip an ECG, or in patients with known structural heart disease, exertional or supine syncope, or age >60 where history alone is unreliable.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Syncope without prodrome plus abnormal ECG, heart disease, exertion, or supine onset should be monitored and evaluated for arrhythmia.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Symptom recall varies with age and questioning; prodrome definitions differ across studies (Berecki-Gisolf pooled 'presence or prolonged presence' of prodrome).

extraction_notes: Estimates 0-2 computed from pooled 2x2 counts in Table 2 of Berecki-Gisolf 2013 (PMC3815402, open access; values read from the XML text dump - the 'Diaphoresis' row's per-study Yes/No sub-columns appear transposed in the dump but the totals 86 (18%) vs 753 (43%) are consistent with the reported LR 1.42). Table's LR column gives the LR for the cardiac-pointing state (absence), which I reproduced as lr_negative; lr_positive is computed. Quotes are verbatim contiguous spans of the table rows. Derivation sample only (not the four test datasets). Estimate 3: Albassam 2019 RCE abstract, prodromal 'feeling cold' (a Calgary-score item); the RCE also lists mood change/preoccupation LR 0.09 (0.02-0.38) and headache LR 0.17 (0.06-0.55) - not entered separately as they do not match this record's title symptoms. Sheldon 2006 (Calgary score) abstract gives only score-level accuracy (89% sens/91% spec) so no estimate; EGSYS abstract lists 'absence of autonomic prodromes' as a predictor without per-item numbers. Situational triggers (micturition, cough, post-prandial) were not separately quantified in accessible sources. Added indication_tags positional, post_prandial.
